mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a reduction in liquidity and an increase in borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by > 0.25% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by > 0.5% in the previous 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS showed a sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a weakening supply side of the economy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by > 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase, it suggests a recovery in the labor market, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending improve.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS increases by > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE was above 7% and PAYEMS increased by > 100k in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust demand environment, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 5% and UNRATE decreases by > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST increased by > 5% and UNRATE decreased by > 0.3% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals inflationary pressures, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the Federal Reserve may tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL increased by > 2% in the previous 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in GDP (GDPC1) indicates a weakening economy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings and economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where GDPC1 decreased by > 1% in the previous quarter.
